- "A computational thalamocortical model found that sleep spindles and slow oscillations promoted replay of awake-learned spike sequences, and memory performance improved after NREM sleep but not after equal awake time [E5]."
- "In 20 healthy adults, EEG sigma power and slow-wave activity during NREM sleep were positively correlated with overnight pre-to-post-sleep consolidation of declarative and procedural memories [E8]."
- "In children and adults performing a motor sequence task, a midday nap produced significant motor-skill gains only at intermediate pre-sleep performance levels [E9]."
